notes: T2-T5 ran R&D 3-4 times per turn without stealing or trashing, so most runs re-accessed the same top card. From T10 to T17 the Runner clicked for credits all turn while sitting on 20-52 credits, and never contested Server 4 while Send a Message (scored T14) and Longevity Serum (advanced T17, game-winning score T18) were advanced there. T9 Pinhole Threading accessed Send a Message and declined to steal.

Every turn from T9 the Runner chose to take a tag with Trickster Taka, then paid a click and 2 credits to remove it (about 15 times). T10, T11, T13 and T15 Stargate runs went into Gatekeeper without breaking it. T14-T22 the Corp sat at 0 credits and could rez nothing, yet the Runner mostly clicked for credits and only won on T28 after milling its stack empty with MaxX. T1 HQ and T2 R&D were facechecks with no breaker.

After IP Block rezzed on Server 1 on T2, the Runner ran into it about 17 more times (T2-T6, T11) with 0 link and no breaker, taking a tag and ending the run every time. It then spent T7-T13 clicking for credits to pay off those tags. The bank went to 0-2 credits while Obokata (T4), SSL Endorsement (T7) and Obokata (T15) were scored unopposed.

Solid pressure with Yusuf on R&D and Archives: stole Project Vitruvius twice (T1-T2), Global Food Initiative from Archives (T5) and Efficiency Committee from Archives to win on T11. Minor oddities: ended T1 at 0 credits, and T9 made two expensive HQ runs through Architect.

T3 facechecked R&D without a killer and lost 4 cards to Anansi. T8 sold Ika to Aesop's Pawnshop and then ran R&D into the known Anansi, losing 4 more cards, although it stole Send a Message. Otherwise a reasonable game that ended with a well-timed T12 run on Server 3 for the win.

T1 made four R&D runs that re-saw the same top card. From T5 to T13 the Runner clicked for credits up to 60 and never installed a breaker. It also left open Archives unchecked from T9 to T13 while the Corp's Asa overwrites were trashing Efficiency Committees there, which were not stolen until T14. T11 (Hagen) and T14 (Vanilla) were runs into ice it had no breaker for, and the Corp won with Global Food Initiative from Vanilla-protected Server 8.

Good early HQ pressure (stole Global Food Initiative and Project Atlas on T2, and Hostile Takeover from Archives on T3), cleared Hard-Hitting News tags sensibly, and won T9 by breaking Border Control with Paperclip to steal Offworld Office. T6 R&D facecheck into Mausolus with 3 credits was loose.

T1 ran into Slot Machine three times and lost all 9 credits. T2 ran R&D at 0 credits into Anansi and lost 4 cards. T4 made four runs at 0 credits into the already-rezzed Border Control. From T5 to T16 it ran HQ every turn into Excalibur plus Border Control with nothing to break them, and the bank never recovered while Obokata, SSL Endorsement and Nisei MK II were scored.

T2-T5 and T7-T8 were spent clicking for credits up to 21 with nothing to spend them on. T9-T12 made 13 runs on Server 4 through Ansel 1.0, whose subroutine forbids stealing, so Global Food Initiative was re-accessed and never stolen. Archives was not checked until T14, although Project Vitruvius and Offworld Office had been sitting in it since the Ansel overwrites.

Fast, aggressive win on T7, stealing five agendas from R&D, HQ and remotes with Black Orchestra and Moshing. Zer0 self-damage trashed useful cards such as Stargate, and the final Fairchild 3.0 run cost 6 credits, but these were acceptable risks at match point.

Good early accesses, including Hyperloop Extension and two Project Vacheron steals, but T7-T10 were spent slowly on economy and draws against a passive Corp. On T12 the Runner ran Archives (taking 4 tags from News Teams) instead of naked Server 1, where Megaprix Qualifier sat and was scored on T13. Won T15 off the Vacheron counters.

T5-T7 made only one R&D run per turn while the Corp idled. T9 ran Server 1 into DNA Tracker with a small grip and lost 3 cards. T11-T15 kept running an empty Archives and clicking for credits. T16 paid 4 for a Paperclip reinstall and still did not break Border Control. T20 ran R&D, Archives and HQ instead of Server 1, where SSL Endorsement scored for the loss on T21.

T2-T4 made 12 R&D runs at 0 credits that mostly re-saw the same top card, and no economy was ever installed (0-2 credits all game). T8, T12 and T13 re-ran Archives into a known News Team, taking 2 tags each time, then spent clicks and credits removing them. Meanwhile the Corp fast-advanced six agendas in new remotes unopposed.

T1-T7 made four R&D runs every turn that re-saw the same top card instead of building money, and the Runner sat at 0-2 credits. The Corp's naked Commercial Bankers Groups and Marilyn Campaigns were never trashed. T8 Stimhacked into Wraparound with no breaker, and T9-T10 were spent removing tags while Degree Mill and Bellona were advanced in Server 9.

Paperclip on Wraparound gave steady HQ access, leading to steals of Remastered Edition (T2), Bellona (T13) and Degree Mill (the T15 win). Economy was very thin for T3-T11, the Runner ran into IP Block on T5 without a breaker, and T11 had to decline Bellona for lack of 5 credits.

T1-T2 made eight R&D runs, most re-seeing the same top card. T5 facechecked Vanilla on Server 4 with no breaker at all. T5-T8 clicked for credits up to 32 without installing a breaker or running HQ or R&D, while the Corp scored Project Vitruvius twice and Global Food Initiative to win on T9.

Sensible Paperclip and D4v1d play: stole SSL Endorsement from HQ (T7) and Nisei from R&D (T8), and won T12 by breaking all three Server 1 ice to take Obokata. Small issues were the T2 HQ facecheck at 0 credits right after the Clone Chip install and the T4 R&D facecheck into Thimblerig.

T2-T6 were 20 straight credit clicks to 28 credits with no runs. T7, T8 (twice), T11, T13 and T15 ran Server 2 through Ansel 1.0 with no sentry breaker, losing Black Orchestra each time and paying the Manegarm 5 to access Cyberdex Sandbox and Offworld Office, which it then declined to steal. Those agendas, plus Global Food Initiative, were all scored from that server.

Clean T5 win: stole Project Vitruvius on T1, then used Dirty Laundry on the fresh Server 1 and Yusuf on Hagen to take two Efficiency Committees on T4, and Global Food Initiative from Server 2 on T5. The T3 facechecks into Hagen and Architect were reasonable early probes.

After T1 the Runner clicked for credits nearly every click through T13, reaching 54 credits, and made only one Archives run. It never trashed the naked Commercial Bankers Groups, Jeeves or Wall to Wall and never pressured HQ or R&D, while the Corp scored Above the Law, Hostile Takeover and two Project Atlas from new remotes.
